key_insight: The folded transonic flutter boundary disappears as the elastic axis moves aft, because supersonic-surface damping falls faster than residual shock energy input.
engineering_relevance: Elastic-axis placement can determine whether multiple flutter thresholds coexist at one Mach number, complicating aeroelastic stability assessment.
method: Coupled unsteady Euler simulations with a Gaussian-process damping surrogate trained by batch active learning.
Used independent simulations for split-conformal calibration of stability calls.
Closed chordwise energy budgets against solver loads and modal growth rates to explain the fold.
evidence_signal: With 80 training simulations, the case A surrogate correctly labeled 64 of 65 independent runs; a broader study using 193 simulations and 40 calibration runs placed fold closure between 0.39 and 0.33 chord ahead of the leading edge on two meshes.
watch_item: Results concern inviscid flow, and damping labels require careful checks: a half-degree mean-incidence offset raised dip flutter speed by 2.8%, exceeding any tested numerical-setting effect.
paper_title: How the elastic axis folds the transonic flutter boundary: shock energy transfer and conformally calibrated active learning
